gross margins, basically a company's revenue for products and services minus the cost spent to deliver that revenue are one of the most important financial metrics in any startup.

key_points.text: But figuring out what does and doesn't go into margins.
key_points.evidence_quote: But figuring out what does and doesn't go into margins, the ideal ratio for a growing business and how this ratio changes from early to later stages of a startup is not as simple as it may sound.

key_points.text: So A16Z general partners, Martin Casado, who invests in early stage enterprise startups, and David George, who leads our our growth fund.
key_points.evidence_quote: So A16Z general partners, Martin Casado, who invests in early stage enterprise startups, and David George, who leads our our growth fund, along with Sarah Wang on the growth investing team, share why margins matter from their vantage points, as well as how modern software business models and technology shifts are changing the way we think about them.

thesis: The speakers argue that gross margins are a critical metric for assessing mature software companies, where high margins (typically 70-80%) enable significant cash flow generation to fund sales, marketing, and engineering. They caution that early-stage margins are often misleading due to the difficulty of distinguishing between fixed infrastructure costs and variable customer-specific costs, noting that margins can shift dramatically as a company matures, as illustrated by Workday's transition from 40% to over 70% margins.
